derivation.surface: mix(base, tube, 0.06); base #0D0A17 for cues and utility, #09070F for record
derivation.ink2: walk mix(mix(tube, #F2EFFA, 0.45), #F2EFFA, t) for t in 0..1 step 0.1 until contrast(surface) >= 4.6; in practice t=0 always clears
derivation.emitted: --surface --tube --tube-rgb --tube-ink --ink --ink-2 --i as inline style per band; --tube-rgb on the stage

notCanonized: secondaryInk's contrast walk never advances: every tube's 45% tint already clears 4.6:1 against its dark surface, so the loop is dead code and --ink-2 is effectively mix(tube, INK, 0.45). Recorded as observed behaviour, not as a rule to depend on.
The warm record band's --ink-2 (#F4EEEC) is indistinguishable from --ink (#F2EFFA). The footer never reads --ink-2 so nothing is visible, but the derivation degrades at the warm stop.
.cue>a:active swaps the hold overlay to rgba(0,0,0,.22), the one black wash in a world whose every other shadow is a tube-colour glow. Press darkens where hover lightens.
The record footer's h2 glow (two layers, no white core) differs from the four-layer recipe used everywhere else; recorded as a variant, not a second recipe to extend.

The rank numeral and Unlisted tag use raw tube colour rather than derived ink; violet #7B5CFF on #140F25 measures 4.28:1, below 4.5:1 for the .82rem rank at the violet stop. Not recorded as an acceptable minimum.
The surface brief's Direction paragraph (.impeccable/surfaces/src-render-html-ts.md) still describes Cyclorama Dawn; it is out of date relative to this build.

narrative.overview:
The contact card is a cue list read down one dark wall of a neon bar. Identity is the sign over the door: the handle set in Tilt Neon and lit magenta. Below it, one lit shelf per app the account has written to. Every shelf is separated from the last by a 2px neon tube whose colour walks cyan to violet to magenta to orange in rank order; the utilities sit under an amber tube and the record footer under a warm white one. Surfaces stay near-black with a faint tint of the tube above them, and light spills from each tube 180px into the shelf below. Colour encodes reading order and nothing else.

Nothing large is solid and saturated. The tubes, the glow around display type, and one magenta button are the only bright fills on the page; everything else is dark surface and light ink. Regions meet at a lit line, never at a hard edge between two flat colours, and nothing casts a shadow: every box-shadow and text-shadow in the world is a zero-offset glow, light emitted rather than light blocked. Type does two jobs: Tilt Neon glows for the sign, the app names and section heads; Saira at 17px with tabular numerals carries everything else in a plain factual register.

The system refuses the link-in-bio scaffold: no avatar circle, no stacked pill buttons, no per-app brand colours or logos, no theme toggle. The avatar is a rectangular photograph in a neon-rimmed frame standing on the first tube at the foot of the first viewport.
keyCharacteristics: Dark tinted surfaces; only the tubes and their glow are bright
Tube colour derived from rank position along a fixed cyan-violet-magenta-orange ramp
Surface, display ink and secondary ink all derived from the tube by fixed mixes
Tilt Neon glowing in tube colour for identity and heads; Saira for everything else
Every shadow is a zero-offset glow; nothing casts
Motion is a stage raise in cue order plus a one-time flicker as the sign ignites; all removed under reduced motion

rules.name: The Rank Ramp Rule
rules.body: A cue's tube is `scale(TUBES, i / (n - 1))` where `TUBES = [cyan, violet, magenta, orange]`, `i` is the app's zero-based rank and `n` the app count; linear RGB interpolation between adjacent stops. One app is cyan; two apps are cyan and orange; four apps land exactly on the four stops. Utilities are always amber, the record footer always warm. Colour never signals importance, only order.

rules.name: The Six Percent Rule
rules.body: A band's surface is its base mixed 6% toward its tube (`mix(SURFACE, tube, 0.06)`; the record footer mixes from the darker record base). That is the whole tint: surfaces never exceed 6% of the tube, and the tube itself never fills an area larger than its 2px line.

rules.name: The Tube Ink Rule
rules.body: Display text lit by a tube is set in the tube mixed 72% toward white (`mix(tube, #FFFFFF, 0.72)`), then glowed with the tube colour. The pale body keeps the glyphs legible (12.9:1 or better on every surface); the tube lives in the shadow layers.

rules.name: The Secondary Ink Rule
rules.body: Secondary ink starts at the tube mixed 45% toward ink and walks toward ink in 10% steps until it reaches 4.6:1 against the surface. On these dark surfaces the first candidate always clears (8:1 or better), so in practice `--ink-2` is `mix(tube, INK, 0.45)`: a tinted ink that carries the tube's hue into the notes and collection names.

rules.name: The Bright Things Rule
rules.body: The only saturated fills on a page are the 2px tubes, the magenta primary button, the selection highlight, and glows. Never fill a band, card, header or footer with a tube colour.

rules.name: The Lit Type Rule
rules.body: Tilt Neon appears only lit: handle, wordmark, app names, section heads, each carrying its tube's glow. It is never set unglowed and never used for body, labels, buttons or numerals.

rules.name: The Neon Glow Recipe
rules.body: A lit heading's `text-shadow` is four layers from a hot core outward: `0 0 1px rgba(255,255,255,.5)`, `0 0 6px tube`, `0 0 18px rgba(tube,.6)`, `0 0 40px rgba(tube,.3)`. The handle scales it up (`1px white .7, 8px, 24px, 64px at .55`); the wordmark drops the white core (`6px, 16px at .7, 34px at .3`); record heads use two layers (`6px at .7, 18px at .35`). Hover on a cue brightens the app name to `1px .8, 8px, 26px .85, 60px .45` over 180ms.

rules.name: The Label-Is-Data Rule
rules.body: Tracked uppercase micro-type appears only as a `<dt>` naming a value, an evidence line naming record collections, a rank numeral, or a status tag. It is never placed above a heading as a kicker or eyebrow.

rules.name: The Tabular Data Rule
rules.body: `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` is set on body and inherited; counts (Apps, Collections, collection totals) are 600 weight so they read as data.

rules.name: The Zero Offset Rule
rules.body: Every shadow is `0 0 <blur>`; nothing has an x or y offset and nothing is black. A shadow with an offset is a cast shadow and does not belong in this world.

rules.name: The Raise Rule
rules.body: Bands enter with `@keyframes raise` (`filter: brightness(.45)` to 1) over 0.8s on `cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1)`, delayed `min(i * 80ms, 640ms) + 120ms` by band index (`--i`) so the wall lights top to bottom. The handle ignites once: `@keyframes ignite`, 1.4s, `steps(1, end)`, opacity `.25, .9, .35, 1, hold, .6, 1` at 0/6/9/12/30/33/35%. Hover transitions are 160–180ms. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` every animation and transition is removed.

dos: Do derive every band's colour from rank with `tubeFor(i, n)` and every surface and ink with `themeFor`; pass them as inline `--surface`, `--tube`, `--tube-rgb`, `--tube-ink`, `--ink`, `--ink-2`, `--i`.
Do keep surfaces dark: a band is its base mixed 6% toward its tube, and the tube is bright only in its 2px line, its glow and its 180px spill.
Do set Tilt Neon only where it glows (handle, wordmark, app names, section heads) in tube ink with the four-layer neon recipe; set everything else in Saira with tabular numerals.
Do make every shadow a zero-offset glow in a tube colour; the hot core, if any, is white at low alpha.
Do mark hover and focus on a cue with the 7% tube hold overlay and a brighter name glow, and focus with a 2px tube-colour outline inset 10px.
Do raise bands in cue order with `--i` delays capped at 640ms, ignite the handle once, and remove all animation and transition under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do mark unrecognised apps with the dashed tube and the Unlisted tag, never by omitting them.
donts: Don't fill a band, header, footer or card with a saturated tube colour; the only saturated fills are the tubes, the magenta primary button, selection and glows.
Don't let two regions meet at a hard edge between flat colours; every seam is a lit tube with spill.
Don't cast a shadow: no offset box-shadow, no black shadow, no long shadow under the actor.
Don't build the link-in-bio scaffold: no avatar circle, no stacked pill buttons, no centred column of equal chips.
Don't give an app its brand colour or logo; tube colour means order, and glyphs are limited to the arrow, search and warning strokes.
Don't place tracked uppercase text above a heading as a kicker or eyebrow; micro-type names a value, a collection, a rank or a status.
Don't hand-assign a surface or ink on a band; every per-band colour is a fixed mix from its tube.
Don't add a theme toggle or a light mode; the room is dark.
Don't use radii above 4px on anything but the step counter circle.
